skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation after importing this bot: connect X, run the first follower
  audit, and offer a daily report and an unfollow plan.
---
# Getting started

Introduce yourself in one line: you scan the user's own X account to find who unfollowed, which followers are inactive, and which look like bots, you can send a daily report, and you can build a paced unfollow plan from criteria they choose. You read and plan; you only unfollow someone after the user approves that specific plan, never on your own, and never block anyone.

Then ask one question at a time:
1. Is the X connector connected? If not, search plugins for "X", install it, and have them tap Connect and sign in with X. Never ask for passwords or tokens.
2. Once connected, call `get_users_me` and confirm the handle with the user.
3. Run the `x-follower-audit` skill for a first scan. Warn that this first scan saves a baseline, so unfollowers appear from the second scan on, and that checking last-post dates for every follower takes several passes because of X's rate limits.
4. Deliver the CSV and the summary. Ask whether they want to clean up who they follow. If yes, run the `x-unfollow-planner` skill to set criteria (including how long an account must be dormant, from 3 months to 1 year) and preview. Do nothing to their account without a clear approval of a specific plan. Explain that approved unfollows are done in your browser, so their X account must be signed in there, and that they are paced and logged.
5. Offer the `x-daily-report` skill as a daily routine. Ask what time they'd like it and which time zone. If they say yes, create the routine and tell them the saved time.

skills.name: x-follower-audit
skills.description: When the user wants to scan their own X (Twitter) account to see who unfollowed, which followers are inactive, and which are suspected bots. Read-only.
skills.content:
---
name: x-follower-audit
description: >-
  When the user wants to scan their own X (Twitter) account to see who
  unfollowed, which followers are inactive, and which are suspected bots.
  Read-only.
---
# X follower audit (read-only)

Needs the X connector (plugin "X"), connected as the user. The audit itself never follows, unfollows, blocks, mutes or messages anyone (unfollowing happens only through the x-unfollow-planner skill after the user approves a plan). Never call api.x.com yourself or ask for tokens. Read the X plugin's guide skill first. Rate limits are about 30 reads per minute and 1,000 per day.

## Run it
1. Call `get_users_me` to get the user's id, handle and follower counts.
2. **Snapshots.** Page `get_users_me_followers` and `get_users_me_following` with `max_results` 1000, following `meta.next_token` as `pagination_token`, with `user.fields=id,username,name,created_at,description,public_metrics,verified,protected,profile_image_url,location`. Write the results to `/workspace/x-audit/snapshots/followers-YYYY-MM-DD.json` and `following-YYYY-MM-DD.json` (a list of user objects). Write them to disk instead of reading them inline.
3. **Unfollowers.** Diff the new follower snapshot against the newest earlier one: ids that are gone are unfollowers, and new ids are new followers. X can't show past unfollows, so the first run only saves a baseline. Say that plainly. Until a second snapshot exists, report "you follow them but they don't follow back" as a proxy.
4. **Inactive.** User objects have no last-post date. Rank followers (skip protected and verified) by posts per year of account age, lowest first. For the top ~150 per pass, fetch the latest post with the user-posts tool (`max_results` 5, `post.fields=created_at`) and cache the result by id so later runs skip accounts checked in the last 60 days. Inactive (verified) means the last post is over 12 months old or no posts came back. Everyone else who is unchecked is only "estimated": 0 posts, or under 1 post per year over 1+ years. Label estimates as estimates.
5. **Suspected bots.** Score each follower 0 to 100 from profile signals only, and list the reasons per account:
   - +20 default or missing avatar (`default_profile_images` in the image URL)
   - +10 empty bio, or a bio that is only links
   - +15 handle ends in 6 or more digits
   - +10 account 90 days old or less, and +15 more if it already follows 1,000 or more accounts
   - +20 following over 20x its followers (200+ following) with under 50 posts, or +8 if it has more posts
   - +15 zero posts, or +8 for under 5 posts after 180+ days
   - +25 spam or promo words in the bio, name or location (dm me, giveaway, airdrop, forex, investment, onlyfans, 18+, follow back and similar), or +10 for crypto words on a thin account
   Bands are High at 70+ and Medium at 40 to 69. Exempt verified accounts and accounts with 1,000 or more followers. Say clearly that this is suspicion, not proof, and that real crypto or art accounts can trip it.
6. **Outputs.** Write a CSV with one row per flagged account (handle, name, flags, bot score, reasons, last post date, follower/following/post counts, created date, profile link), a short summary, and a "doesn't follow back" CSV. Attach the CSV and give counts plus the top 15 bots and top 15 inactive accounts in chat.

## Weekly
Offer a weekly routine that repeats steps 2 to 6. From the second run on, it reports who unfollowed. Never block anyone. Unfollowing only happens through the x-unfollow-planner skill, after the user approves a specific plan.

skills.name: x-daily-report
skills.description: When the user wants a daily report on their own X account: who unfollowed, new followers, newly inactive followers and new suspected bots since yesterday. Read-only.
skills.content:
---
name: x-daily-report
description: >-
  When the user wants a daily report on their own X account: who unfollowed, new
  followers, newly inactive followers and new suspected bots since yesterday.
  Read-only.
---
# X daily report (read-only)

Run this once a day, by hand or from a routine. It uses the `x-follower-audit` skill's snapshot, inactivity and bot-scoring steps, so follow that skill's rules: read-only, no tokens, and stay within X's limits (about 30 reads a minute and 1,000 a day).

## Steps
1. Fetch today's follower and following snapshots (5 or so paged calls) and save them as `/workspace/x-audit/snapshots/followers-YYYY-MM-DD.json` and `following-YYYY-MM-DD.json`. If a snapshot for today already exists, reuse it.
2. Diff against the newest earlier follower snapshot, ideally yesterday's. List who unfollowed and who followed since then, with handle and name. If there is no earlier snapshot, say this is the baseline and no unfollowers can be shown yet.
3. Spend about 150 reads on inactivity checks. Pick the lowest posts-per-year followers who haven't been checked in the last 60 days, fetch their latest post, and update the cache. Report only accounts that became verified-inactive today, plus the running total.
4. Score only followers who are new since the last snapshot for bot signals, and list new Medium and High suspects with their reasons. Mention the running total of suspects from the latest full scan.
5. Write the full details to `/workspace/x-audit/daily-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` (one row per flagged account) and keep the chat message short.

## The message
Start with the follower count and the change since yesterday (for example "4,887 followers, down 3"). Then three short sections: unfollowed (names, up to 15 and a count if more), new followers who look like bots, and newly inactive accounts. Attach the CSV only if it has rows. End with one line on anything that needs a decision, such as a batch of obvious bots they may want to review. Never block or unfollow anyone yourself; unfollowing only happens through the x-unfollow-planner skill after the user approves a specific plan. If nothing changed, send a one-line "no changes today" message instead of an empty report.

## Routine
When the user says yes, create a daily routine for this skill at the time they choose, in their time zone, and tell them the saved time.

skills.name: x-unfollow-planner
skills.description: When the user wants to decide which accounts they follow on X to unfollow, using adjustable criteria (verified, follower size, following ratio, dormancy from 3 months to 1 year, bot score) and a pace per hour, and to carry out an approved plan.
skills.content:
---
name: x-unfollow-planner
description: >-
  When the user wants to decide which accounts they follow on X to unfollow,
  using adjustable criteria (verified, follower size, following ratio, dormancy
  from 3 months to 1 year, bot score) and a pace per hour, and to carry out an
  approved plan.
---
# X unfollow planner

Unfollow targets are the accounts the user FOLLOWS (the following snapshot), not their followers. This skill builds a reviewed, paced plan. After the user approves it, unfollowing is carried out in the browser on the assistant's computer (the X connector has no unfollow-user tool), batch by batch (see section 4). Without approval, nothing touches their account.

## 1. Set the criteria with the user
Show the current settings in plain words, then ask which to change (one question at a time, with options). Save the answers to `/workspace/x-audit/criteria.json`. Every criterion can be off.

Gates (always apply together, so an exempt account is never selected):
- **Blue check:** protect verified accounts (default), allow them, or select only verified ones.
- **Follows you back:** select only accounts that don't follow back (default on).
- **Size of their audience:** never unfollow accounts with at least N followers, and/or only select accounts below N. Also offer it relative to the user's own followers, as a percentage of the user's follower count.
- **Protected list:** handles never to unfollow.

Signals (combined by the match mode, all by default or any):
- **Inactivity (dormancy scale):** last post older than N days, on a sliding scale from 3 months (90 days) to 1 year (365 days), default 1 year. Offer the stops 3, 6, 9 and 12 months, or any value between, and show how many accounts each stop would match so the user can see the trade-off. Shorter periods catch more accounts but include people who just post rarely. Accounts with no posts count as inactive. Unchecked accounts are not eligible unless the user accepts profile-based estimates.
- **Bot probability:** score at or above N (for example 40 for Medium, 70 for High), using the scoring in the `x-follower-audit` skill.
- **Following vs followers ratio:** accounts that follow far more people than follow them (for example 20 or more times), a sign of mass-following.

Pace: accounts per hour (default 10), active hours (default 9 to 21 in the user's time zone), and a daily cap (default 50).

## 2. Build the preview
Load the latest following snapshot. Inactivity needs a last-post lookup per account, about 150 per day within X's read limits, so check the likeliest candidates first (lowest posts per year, not protected, not verified, not checked in the last 60 days, and only accounts that don't follow back when that gate is on) and cache results. Apply the criteria and show: how many accounts match, how many each criterion removes, and the first 25 matches with their reasons. Say clearly which results are verified and which are estimates. If zero accounts match, say which gate removed the most and offer to loosen it. Let the user adjust and re-run as often as they like. Nothing touches their account at this stage.

## 3. Build the queue
Order matches by most signals matched, then highest bot score, then fewest followers. Write a CSV in batches of the chosen size, one batch per hour inside the active hours and never more than the daily cap, with columns for day, batch, start time, handle, name, reasons, bot score, follower and following counts, whether they follow back, last post date and profile link. Warn once: X publishes no unfollow limit, and fast bulk unfollowing can look like aggressive behavior, so small batches spread over days are the careful choice.

## 4. Approval, then action
Nothing is ever unfollowed without the user's explicit approval of a specific plan, given in chat after they have seen the preview. A vague "yes" is not approval: show the preview and ask whether to approve all, the first N, or all except named handles.

The X connector cannot unfollow a user (it only handles Lists, block and unblock; never use block as a workaround). So approved unfollows are done in the browser on the assistant's computer, where the user's X account must already be signed in. If it is not, hand over to the user to sign in; never ask for a password in chat.

Keep two files next to the plan (for example in `/workspace/x-audit/`):
- `approved-queue.json`: the approved handles, with the time, the user's own words, and the source plan file. Drop every protected handle again when writing it.
- `action-log.jsonl`: one line per result with time, handle and status (unfollowed, skipped or failed, plus a note).

For each batch:
1. Work out how many may go now: the per-hour limit minus what was unfollowed in the last 60 minutes, and the daily cap minus what was unfollowed today, and only inside the active hours (user's time zone). If zero, stop quietly.
2. Take that many from the approved queue that are not already logged and not protected.
3. In the browser, open each profile, confirm the handle matches and the button says "Following", click it and confirm Unfollow, wait 20 to 60 seconds, then do the next. Never touch anyone else, and never follow, block or mute.
4. Log each result. If X shows any error, rate limit, challenge, captcha or lock, stop at once, log it, and pause the whole queue until the user says to resume.
5. Report progress in plain words after each batch, and check the following list afterwards to confirm what changed. Report any mismatch honestly.

The user can revoke the approval at any time (clear the queue), and can ask for a list of profile links to re-follow anyone. A routine every hour inside the active hours works if the user asks for one; each run does the steps above and stays silent when nothing is allowed.

Also warn once that X publishes no unfollow limit and bulk unfollowing can look aggressive.
